title: autosurgeon: deterministic rollback planner with adaptive holdpoints and staged A/B reconciliation
author: Priya Nair
description: Motivation: We need a deterministic planner that schedules automated rollbacks and staged reconciliations for multi-variant rollouts (A/B) while minimizing user-visible disruption. Existing rollout controllers at Redwood focus on fraction-based traffic phasing and metric gates but do not produce reproducible rollback plans or a reproducible dry-run output that operators can audit before promotion. This PR introduces 'Autosurgeon', a rollback planner that (1) computes a canonical rollback path given observed metrics and holdpoint signals, (2) inserts adaptive holdpoints when risk exceeds a threshold, and (3) supports staged A/B reconciliation where variants are reconciled in a dependency graph rather than flat fractions. Summary of changes: 1) New package orchestration/autosurgeon: planner, simulator, policy adapters. Planner is deterministic: given the same metrics snapshot and policy-as-data input it yields the same sequence of actions (traffic adjustments, quarantine, revert, promote). 2) Holdpoint scoring engine: computes a per-cohort score using latency, error-rate, and a synthetic quality metric. Scores map to three actions: continue, hold-and-observe, trigger-rollback. 3) A/B reconciliation graph: declarative DAG that expresses variant dependencies and reconciliation windows. 4) Simulator CLI (bin/autosurgeon-sim) that consumes past telemetry and produces a replay of actions for operator review. 5) Integrations: a) Console UI hook (rollouts tab) to preview the planned rollback steps, b) webhook event sink to emit planned actions for audit/playbook integration, c) compact protobuf for planner output used by dedicated and private runtimes. Motivation/Context: This addresses on-call incidents where rollbacks oscillated because the previous controller made reactive fraction changes without a reproducible plan; operators lacked a way to simulate the plan before executing it. Design notes: - Determinism is achieved by using a single monotonic scoring and tie-breaker rule-set (timestamp + stable variant ordering). - Holdpoints are adaptive: if a metric crosses a dynamic threshold (baseline + ridge margin) a holdpoint is inserted and an observation window is scheduled. - Reconciliation graph supports upstream/downstream consistency (useful when model A depends on feature-extractor B). - Planner supports two execution modes: dry-run (no traffic changes, only plan emitted) and execute (applies actions via the existing routing layer). Checklist: - [x] Planner implementation + unit tests - [x] Simulator and sample telemetry recorder - [x] Console preview endpoint and minimal UI stub - [x] E2E smoke test against perf-canary harness - [x] Documentation: design doc, runbook, and operator checklist - [x] Backwards-compatible output protobuf (v1 -> v2 shim) How to review: Focus review on the planner logic in orchestration/autosurgeon/planner.go, the holdpoint scoring utils, and the reconciliation DAG emitter. The simulator contains the easiest-to-follow end-to-end path: run bin/autosurgeon-sim --telemetry sample/telemetry-2026-01.json --policy samples/policy.yaml to produce a reproducible plan. Running tests: make test-unit ./orchestration/autosurgeon && make test-e2e ./test/e2e-rollouts. Rollout plan for merging: This is flagged for a gradual rollout: the feature gate is off by default. We will enable dry-run mode for all accounts for 48 hours, collect operator feedback, then enable execute mode for internal teams, and finally enable for all customers behind a tenant opt-in. Related: ENG-2028 (planner core), ENG-2035 (console preview), linked docs: designs/autosurgeon.md and runbooks/rollback-planner-playbook.md. Breaking changes: none expected; protobuf is additive and includes a compatibility shim. Notes: The protobuf serialization was kept compact to avoid increasing on-wire traffic for hosted API. For private installs, the CLI can operate in offline dry-run mode using exported telemetry snapshots. Release notes: "Adds Autosurgeon rollback planner: deterministic rollback planning, adaptive holdpoints, and a simulator for safe dry-run auditing of multi-variant rollouts."

review_comments: Owen Michaels: Nice isolation between planner and execution layer. One question: are there any race conditions if two planners run concurrently for the same rollout?

Priya Nair: We added a lease around the execution phase; the planner can run concurrently in dry-run mode. Only the executor will acquire the lease before making routing changes. Updated planner.go with LeaseManager usage.
Sofia Park: Can we reduce the default observation window from 10m to 5m for low-traffic cohorts? Suggested a cadence override in policy.yaml.
Priya Nair: Agreed, added a per-cohort window override and documentation describing trade-offs.
Diego Alvarez: CI flaky on the e2e job first run (timeout). Reran and it passed. Consider making the perf-canary fixture deterministic for the sim tests.
Priya Nair: Increased timeouts and seeded the perf-canary fixture RNG to make the sim deterministic. CI green on rerun.
release_notes: Adds Autosurgeon rollback planner (deterministic rollback plans, adaptive holdpoints, staged A/B reconciliation) + simulator CLI for dry-run auditing. Feature gate off by default; rollout staged per runbook.
testing_notes: Unit tests cover scoring thresholds, DAG generation, and tie-breaker determinism. E2E smoke test runs the simulator against a stored telemetry snapshot and verifies the plan is idempotent when replayed. Manual test: run bin/autosurgeon-sim --telemetry samples/telemetry-2026-01.json and validate console preview endpoint shows identical steps.
notes_for_oncall: If the planner issues unexpected rollback actions, flip feature.gates.autosurgeon.execute=false to stop active execution. Use bin/autosurgeon-sim --telemetry <snapshot> to reproduce planner decisions locally. The runbook docs/runbooks/rollback-planner-playbook.md contains play-by-play mitigation steps and audit queries.
